title: Cloud Shelf Governance and Go‑Live Sprint Plan
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a tactical runbook for final governance checks, copy freeze, and the 3-week sprint to land our cloud marketplace listings across AWS/Azure/GCP. Intended audience: GTM PM, Marketplace ops, Legal, Security, Solution Engineering, and Partner Success.

Scope (what we will ship):
- Marketplace tiles for AWS, Azure, GCP with consistent SKUs and trial entitlements
- One consolidated short description + two long-form variants (enterprise + developer)
- Compliance checklist (KMS, data residency call-outs where applicable)
- Technical acceptance tests and a post-launch rollback plan

Summary timeline (high-level):
Week 0 (pre-sprint): copy drafts + legal flagging
Week 1: technical acceptance + imagery and asset upload to vendor portals
Week 2: internal QA, pricing alignment, legal/finance signoff
Week 3: partner go-live window + monitoring runbook activation

Launch dependencies (must-have before submission):
- Billing SKU mapping approved by Finance (owner: Arjun) — Jira: JIRA-BILL-114
- Security packaging sign-off: data flow diagram + KMS integration notes (owner: Liam)
- One-pager and trial entitlements finalized (owner: Maya)
- Vendor portal accounts active for each cloud (owner: PM E2E)

Acceptance criteria (technical):
- Listing returns valid redirect and tile metadata via portal APIs
- Free trial provisioning completes within 2 minutes for sample account
- Landing page links (docs, pricing, contact) are resolved with 200 status
- Logged metric: first-call latency for hosted API sample <= 250ms median (measured from portal test harness)

Acceptance criteria (copy/marketing):
- Short description <= 300 characters, emphasizes "predictable inference" and "deployment flexibility"
- Long description includes 3 bullet-value props: cost-control, SLA-backed Dedicated, private deployment options
- At least one customer use-case example (SaaS conversational assistant) with privacy note

Marketplace-specific notes (quick):
- AWS: ensure Marketplace listing includes AMI/bring-your-own mapping if Dedicated offered; list support SLA levels
- Azure: confirm ARM template and managed offer metadata; verify Azure Marketplace pricing unit aligns to our per-hour reserved capacity SKU
- GCP: add region and VPC connectivity notes for Private deployments; include contact for on-prem evaluation

Governance checklist (legal & security quick pass):
- [ ] Standard MSA clause version referenced (link: CONFLUENCE-1234)
- [ ] Data residency statement drafted for EU customers
- [ ] KMS/HSM integration notes included in listing assets
- [ ] PII handling guidance included in docs links
- [ ] Vulnerability disclosure and incident response contact added to portal support contact

Copy variants (working text snippets) — pick one short + one long:
- Short candidate A: "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and lower unit cost — hosted API, reserved Dedicated pools, or private VPC deployments."
- Short candidate B: "High-performance inference for production apps: fast SDKs, configurable capacity, and built-in cost controls."
- Long candidate (developer): "Redwood Inference gives engineering teams a single API and runtime for serving large language models across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Optimize latency and cost with intelligent batching, KV cache, and model routing. Integrates with KMS for secure key storage and supports canary rollouts for safe releases."
- Long candidate (enterprise): "Redwood provides SLA-backed Dedicated capacity and private deployment options for regulated workloads. Our platform focuses on predictable inference economics — enabling teams to control per-token cost while maintaining production quality via rollouts, observability, and fallback policies."

Image and asset checklist:
- [ ] Tile artwork (square) – 1200x1200, acceptable by all portals
- [ ] Promotional banner (landscape) – 1200x300
- [ ] PDF one-pager (technical + pricing)
- [ ] Architecture diagram SVG (KMS, VPC notes)

Ops + monitoring (post-launch):
- Enable Console dashboard: set alert for 3x baseline token cost or 2x latency SLO violations in first 72h
- Partner Success to standby for first 2 business days after go-live
- Track conversion funnel from marketplace trial -> paid over first 30 days

Submission QA checklist (portal-specific):
- [ ] Metadata fields validated (short/long descriptions copied exactly)
- [ ] Pricing table matches Finance-approved SKUs
- [ ] Legal contact info filled, support SLA reference added
- [ ] Screenshots uploaded and links verified
- [ ] Terms and licensing checkbox validated by Legal

Risks & mitigations (fast list):
- Risk: Pricing unit mismatch between portals. Mitigation: canonical SKU mapping doc + final Finance sign-off
- Risk: Portal review takes longer than expected. Mitigation: stagger submissions and request expedited review from partner manager
- Risk: Security packaging flagged. Mitigation: pre-submit vulnerability summary and remediation ETA

Open items (owner — due):
- Finalize short description (Maya — 2026-03-12)
- Confirm AMI/bundling approach for Dedicated (Infra SE — 2026-03-15)
- Draft data residency language for EU/Germany (Legal — 2026-03-13)
- Upload tile art and architecture diagram (Design — 2026-03-11)

Playbook snippets (how to handle rollback):
- If portal validation fails critical (security/legal): pause publication, revert to previous internal listing, notify partners@redwood and open JIRA GO-LIVE-ROLLBACK.
- If post-launch latency spikes: enable automatic fallback to low-cost model variant and notify SRE, enable scaling policy for Dedicated fleets.

Notes / sticky thoughts (informal):
- We should avoid overloaded marketing terms like "enterprise-grade" without measurable hooks (SLA numbers / percent uplift).
- Consider a short "what to expect during trial" card for marketplace tile to reduce support ticket volume.
- Ask Finance if we can publish a visible free-tier token allotment vs trial requiring contact form.

Appendix: Quick links & references:
- Confluence: go-live checklist (CONFLUENCE-1234)
- Jira epic: JIRA-GO-LIVE-89
- PR with assets: https://github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-assets/pull/42
